scope: Architecture sources only; no production source registration and no new scientific effect claims.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Primer (Second Edition)
claimsSupported: Categories/classes differ from particular individuals.
Missing assertions under open-world semantics are not false assertions.
OWL is not a syntax-presence validator.
sources.designUse: Type/occurrence distinction; retain explicit unknown coverage alongside closed-world JSON validation.
sources.limitations: No claim that PSYWERX implements OWL semantics or needs an OWL store.

sources.title: Semantic Sensor Network Ontology
sources.organization: W3C and OGC Spatial Data on the Web Working Group
claimsSupported: An actuation performs a procedure on a property of a feature of interest.
Observation, actuation, procedure, and result have distinct roles.
sources.designUse: Reusable specification versus performed episode versus recorded result.
sources.limitations: Sensor and actuator assumptions are narrower than human organizations or disasters; observation does not prove downstream causation.

sources.title: Time Ontology in OWL
claimsSupported: Instants, intervals, duration, and temporal position are distinct.
Before/after and interval overlap describe temporal ordering.
sources.designUse: Separate episode timing from causal lag and exposure-pattern descriptors.
sources.limitations: Ordering does not establish causality. Latest unversioned page was a 2022 Candidate Recommendation Draft; this register pins the 2017 Recommendation.

sources.title: Environmental conditions, treatments and exposures ontology (ECTO)
claimsSupported: Exposure can be represented as receptor–stressor interaction with medium and route.
Composable descriptions avoid requiring a prebuilt class for each combination.
sources.designUse: Exposure profile with recipient, input, route, and pattern; domain tags may overlap.
sources.limitations: Organism-centered examples do not settle social/institutional semantics. README warns about release stability; no ECTO import is proposed.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
claimsSupported: Entities, activities, agents, derivation, attribution, and revision describe provenance.
Qualified relations permit additional attribution/role/context details.
sources.designUse: Record extraction, synthesis, simulation, review actor, source revision, and exact assertion revision separately.
sources.limitations: Provenance influence/derivation is not scientific causal evidence or a PSYWERX RDS derivation rule.

sources.title: SEPIO Core Information Model: Statement and EvidenceLine documentation
claimsSupported: Evidence is assessed against a particular proposition.
Evidence direction and strength are separate; multiple evidence items may support one argument.
Qualifiers constrain statement scope.
sources.designUse: Preserve source-level findings before assertion-level synthesis.
sources.limitations: Legacy OWL repository is explicitly outdated. Do not copy optional numeric scores or use both duplicate statement encoding patterns.

sources.title: Causal inference in statistics: An overview
claimsSupported: Causal inference requires explicit assumptions beyond statistical association.
Exogenous variables are defined relative to a model; they need not be mutually independent.
Model graphs encode substantive exclusion assumptions.
sources.designUse: Separate association and causal claims; record model assumptions; external-to-actor does not mean unconfounded.
sources.limitations: An incomplete catalog is not a complete causal model: absent PSYWERX edges cannot be interpreted as zero influence. No identification algorithm is adopted.

sources.title: On the distinction between interaction and effect modification
claimsSupported: Effect modification concerns one intervention's effect varying across another variable's strata; interaction concerns two interventions' effects.
sources.designUse: Separate moderator conditions from claims that manipulating the moderator changes the mechanism.
sources.limitations: Abstract-level review only; PubMed lists 2010 and 2011 errata. No detailed estimators or numeric rules borrowed.

sources.title: American Statistical Association Releases Statement on Statistical Significance and P-Values
reviewedSections: Complete three-page announcement including six principles
claimsSupported: Statistical significance does not measure effect size or hypothesis truth.
Scientific conclusions require context and full reporting, not a p-value threshold alone.
sources.designUse: Record null findings with estimand, uncertainty, and limits; never convert nonsignificance to zero effect.
sources.limitations: The linked journal article was not reviewed in full; this source is the association's own announcement, not a PSYWERX confidence rubric.

accessLimitations: Selected normative/documentation sections were inspected; no claim to full review of every standard.
Two PMC direct-access attempts returned browser verification pages and were not used as evidence.
VanderWeele access was PubMed abstract/metadata; detailed estimation methods and errata content were not reviewed.
Mutable maintainer pages are access-date snapshots, not pinned dependency releases.
